COBIT 2019 — governance objectives and Managed Data (COBIT 2019 (EDM01-05,
One assessment, three vocabularies. These are not three independent measurements — they are one evidence base expressed in three
published frameworks. The three overall figures landing close together is the CORRECT result: the same answers, projected through the same
35 TACR sections. What differs between them is emphasis and structure, which is what makes each one legible to a different audience.
RETAINED SHARE is how much of the framework’s own definition of a dimension is in scope for this assessment. SCORED SHARE is how
much of what is in scope was actually measured. They answer different questions and are never combined: a dimension can be fully retained
and barely scored, or the reverse, and a single "coverage" number would hide whichever is worse.
RETAINED SHARE here is structural, not scope-driven. This assessment has no core/banking split, so a leaf dimension is either fully mapped
(100% retained) or mapped by nothing at all (0%, and reported as NOT APPLICABLE rather than scored). A framework’s own retained share
falls below 100% precisely when one of its leaves is unreachable from this assessment. Where the two shares diverge on a leaf, the cause is
always what has been ANSWERED, never what is in scope.
A dimension is SCORED, NOT ASSESSED or NOT APPLICABLE, and the last two never render as 0. "Not assessed" means the framework
defines it, it is in scope, and nobody has answered the questions behind it yet. "Not applicable" means this assessment asks nothing that could
evidence it. A zero would read as "measured, and bad" for both.
All figures are on the TAIW 1-5 maturity scale. They are NOT rescaled to each framework’s own scale — DCAM scores 1-6 and COBIT 2019
uses capability levels 0-5. A DCAM component shown here as 3.2 is 3.2 out of 5, not out of 6.
What is published and what is ours
Framework names, codes and dimension structures are PUBLISHED content. The relative WEIGHTS applied to those
dimensions are Godaitec editorial judgement — none of these frameworks publishes weightings for its own dimensions. The
weights are the first thing to challenge in review, and changing them changes every figure derived from them.
COBIT2019 (COBIT 2019 (EDM01-05, APO14)) — Published structure recorded at MEDIUM confidence — verify before relying on it in an audit
The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence, including EDM05 'Ensured Stakeholder Engagement' (renamed from COBIT 5's
'Ensure Stakeholder Transparency'). APO14 Managed Data was new in COBIT 2019 and carries ten management practices
APO14.01-APO14.10. The titles below were originally paraphrased from memory; they have since been checked against a public COBIT
2019 reference and two were corrected (APO14.03 lost a stray 'the', APO14.08 now reads 'life cycle' as two words). They have NOT been
checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — that verification is still outstanding
and is why structureConfidence stays at medium rather than rising. COBIT 2019 capability levels run 0-5, which is why scaleMin is 0 and not
1. Giving APO14 55% of the framework weight is DGIW's judgement: it is the only data-specific objective in COBIT, so a COBIT-framed DATA
assessment cannot sensibly be dominated by the generic governance domain.
What TAIW's assessment can and cannot evidence
DGI IS NOT OFFERED. DGI reaches 59% of itself on TACR. Decision Rights, Accountabilities, the Data Governance Office and Data
Stewards are mapped by nothing, because a customs assessment does not ask who chairs a data governance council. A DGI score built on
the 59% that does map would carry an invisible 41% gap, so DGI is not offered at all. The four dimensions it loses are Decision Rights,
Accountabilities, Data Governance Office, Data Stewards — which is close to a definition of what DGI is. This is a finding about TACR, not a

defect in DGI: the same ten DGI leaves reach 100% of themselves on HAIW's HACR subcategories.
DM07 IS NOT APPLICABLE. Document & Content Management. 0 of 640 TACR questions mention document or content management.
Customs runs on declarations, manifests and certificates, so this is a real gap in the ASSESSMENT rather than an absence in the domain —
and forcing it onto Clearance Automation would be a mapping nobody could defend. HAIW does not share it: DM07 lands on
ii_document_exchange there, because health runs on clinical documents.
THREE FRAMEWORKS, NOT FOUR. Every figure on this document is a projection of ONE TACR assessment onto DMBOK2, DCAM and
COBIT 2019. Nothing here is a second opinion; the frameworks cannot corroborate one another because they are reading the same

Retained and scored share are SEPARATE columns on purpose. Retained is how much of the framework’s own definition this assessment
covers; scored is how much of that was measured. Combining them would hide whichever is worse.

None. Every leaf dimension of COBIT2019 is either mapped in full or mapped by nothing — there is no scope filter on this
assessment that could retain part of one. COBIT2019's own retained share of 100% above is the weighted mean over its 15
leaves, and it falls below 100% exactly when one of them is unreachable, which is listed under "Not applicable" below.

Why each dimension maps to the TACR sections it does
Every row below was authored deliberately. A mapping a consultant cannot defend in a room is not a mapping, and this section is the room.
EDM01 · Ensured Governance Framework Setting and Maintenance
A documented strategy aligned with national trade policy objectives, actively driving decisions, is
the governance framework EDM01 requires to be set and maintained.
Formal alignment across Customs, FBR and the Ministry of Commerce, plus WCO and WTO
committee participation, is the maintenance half — governance held in place by standing
Revenue tracked against approved targets, leakage quantified with reduction targets, and duty
recovery measurably improved by data-driven intervention: benefits, delivered and evidenced.
Clearance times measured by WCO Time Release Study and shown to have decreased as a
documented result of reform is the facilitation half of the same benefit case.
EDM03 is ENTERPRISE risk governance, not customs targeting. The cybersecurity strategy
aligned with national frameworks, endpoint protection and intrusion detection are TACR's
A documented disaster recovery plan with agreed, tested RTO/RPO and a geographically
separated site is the other half of enterprise risk optimisation.
A comprehensive workforce capacity assessment aligned with modernization needs, and strategic
workforce planning tied to the roadmap, is resource optimisation in its most direct form.
Whether dedicated data science posts exist and whether analysts hold modelling skills is the
Data centre and storage capacity adequate for current and projected need is resource optimisation

Structured private-sector consultation in modernization planning, and active WCO/WTO
cooperation, is stakeholder engagement as EDM05 defines it.
Trader satisfaction surveys with representative sampling, analysed into prioritised action plans, is

The digital vision section carries the strategy-and-communication half: articulated vision,
Ownership, stewardship and approval workflows are the roles-and-responsibilities half, and TACR
MOUs defining scope, formats and update frequencies assign responsibilities across organisational
APO14.02 · Define and maintain a consistent business glossary
WCO Data Model element mapping and message implementation profiles are the controlled
vocabulary Pakistan Customs actually maintains; a customs administration's business glossary is
TACR's single catalogue question sits in the warehouse section. THIS IS THIN — one question in
640 — and the score should be read as indicative rather than measured.
APO14.03 · Establish processes and infrastructure for metadata management
Maintaining WCO DM mappings and MIPs across WeBOC, PSW and partner systems is metadata
management performed against a standard, whatever it is called locally.
Lineage and catalogue questions in the warehouse section are the infrastructure half. Same

APO14.04 · Define a data quality strategy
Data quality rules defined and documented for all critical customs data elements is the strategy this
APO14.05 · Establish data profiling methodologies, processes and tools
Automated validation at the point of entry, and metrics monitored against defined thresholds, is
Profiling needs a platform to run on; pipeline monitoring is where systematic profiling would be
APO14.06 · Ensure a data quality assessment approach
Quality metrics monitored through operational dashboards against defined acceptable thresholds is
an assessment approach, not just a rule set.
Scheduled automated reporting is how a quality assessment reaches the people who act on it.
APO14.07 · Define the data cleansing approach
Validation at entry prevents the defects a cleansing approach would otherwise have to remove;
Harmonising and synchronising reference codes across systems is cleansing applied to the data
APO14.08 · Manage the life cycle of data assets
Retention questions in the privacy section are where TACR asks about the end of the lifecycle.
Storage adequate for long-term retention is the infrastructure the lifecycle runs on.
Tariff codes managed with full change history is lifecycle management applied to reference data.

APO14.09 · Support data archiving and retention
Storage capacity for growing volumes and long-term retention needs is the archiving question TACR
Retention policy sits with data protection here. TACR has no question containing "archive"; this
dimension is inferred from retention and storage, and its score should be read accordingly.
APO14.10 · Manage data backup and restore arrangements
A one-to-one match. Documented DR plan, agreed and tested RTO/RPO, and a geographically
separated site with replicated data is backup and restore as COBIT scopes it.

What this assessment does not cover
Every leaf dimension of COBIT2019 is in scope and measured. Nothing in the framework is unaddressed. Read that against the
instrument qualification above rather than as depth.
Dimensions scored from part of their evidence
None. Every dimension that is scored at all is scored from every TACR section mapped to it.
7 of 35 TACR sections are reached by none of the 3 frameworks. They are still SCORED on the assessment and they still
appear in TAIW's own maturity report — they simply contribute to no framework scorecard, because no published
These are customs operations rather than data management: TFA commitments, clearance and revenue automation, risk models, compliance
rates and officer training. No published data-management framework defines them, and mapping them onto one anyway would be a mapping
nobody could defend in a room. They are measured, they carry a maturity score, and they appear in the TAIW maturity report — they are simply
outside what DMBOK2, DCAM and COBIT 2019 are about. WTO TFA Commitment is the clearest case: it is eighteen questions, one per TFA
Article, so the framework’s vocabulary IS the assessment and a projection would restate it against itself.
DCAM is modelled at v2.2. Its capability and sub-capability levels beneath each component are deliberately NOT authored: they were not
recalled reliably enough to put in front of an auditor, and an absent level is recoverable where an invented one is not. DCAM v3.0
reorganised the model and is not what is represented here.
COBIT 2019 APO14 sub-practice titles have been checked against a public COBIT 2019 reference and corrected where they differed. They
have NOT been checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — treat them as
verified secondhand, not as quoted. The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence.
